record.paper_title: Some results and open problems in research on low dimensional organic conductors
record.original_question: What is the origin of high-temperature superconductivity? In the context of this review, the question is whether insights from low-dimensional organic conductors, fulleride-based conductors, and high-Tc materials can be integrated into a definitive explanation of the mechanism responsible for high-temperature superconductivity.

evidence.quote: In spite of world-wide efforts, the problem of the origin of high temperature superconductivity still evades a definitive solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Identify the microscopic pairing mechanism responsible for high-temperature superconductivity. Specifically, formulate a unified theoretical framework — for instance, a many-body Hamiltonian on a lattice together with an effective pairing interaction — that simultaneously accounts for the superconducting phases observed in (i) quasi-low-dimensional organic conductors (such as Bechgaard and Fabre salts of the (TMTSF)_2X and (TMTTF)_2X families and BEDT-TTF based κ-phase salts), (ii) alkali-doped fulleride conductors A_3C_60, and (iii) cuprate and related high-Tc superconductors. The framework should predict the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter, the dependence of the critical temperature T_c on control parameters (pressure, doping, dimensionality, bandwidth), and the proximity of the superconducting phase to competing instabilities (antiferromagnetic, charge-density-wave, spin-density-wave, or Mott-insulating phases). Determine whether a single non-phononic (e.g. electronic, magnetic) pairing mechanism, a conventional electron–phonon mechanism, or a combination thereof can quantitatively reproduce the observed phenomenology across all three classes of materials.
artifact.status_search_result: The mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity remains a celebrated open problem in condensed matter and mathematical physics. Despite decades of intensive theoretical and experimental work, no consensus microscopic theory has been established that uniformly explains pairing in cuprates, organic conductors, and fullerides.

status_evidence.title: High-temperature superconductivity
status_evidence.snippet: The mechanism by which high-temperature superconductors operate is still not known.
status_evidence.claim: The pairing mechanism for high-Tc superconductivity is still not established.

status_evidence.snippet: Understanding the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity in the cuprates remains one of the major outstanding problems of condensed matter physics.
status_evidence.claim: Understanding high-Tc superconductivity remains a major open problem.
